title: The Locker of Cedar Falls
premise: Ines Amberdale arrives in Cedar Falls insisting everything is fine, but the school sits atop a drowned town whose residents were never given justice. When he finds his grandmother's recipe box hiding instructions for unlocking memories sealed inside locker 117, he discovers she was one of the kids who covered up a death decades ago. To set things right, Ines must win both the state swim championship and the trust of the ghost-students who remember everything — before the school board demolishes the old wing and erases them forever. He wins neither race cleanly but exposes the truth at the meet itself, and the found family of living and dead students finally gets their names read aloud.
about_author: Noor Hartwell is a former small-town lifeguard who grew up swimming in pools built over forgotten places. They write YA stories about stubborn kids, buried histories, and the families we assemble on purpose.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. New town, new school, grandma's spare room, and a recipe box that smells like lake water. A card labeled 'For the championship' contains no food — just coordinates and a name: Marisol Vann, 1974. Ines follows it to locker 117, which is warm to the touch. Emotional beat: denial cracking into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Kept Score
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with interludes from Marisol's recovered memories. The lockers hold the memories of students erased after Marisol's drowning was ruled an accident that three classmates witnessed. Ines recruits swim-team outcast Dev and janitor Mr. Okafor, who has been leaving flowers by locker 117 for years. Emotional beat: loneliness giving way to alliance.

chapters.title: Splits
chapters.summary: Dual POV — Ines racing qualifiers while Dev digs through county archives. The demolition order moves up two weeks; the memories will be destroyed with the wall. Grandma, lucid for one afternoon, confesses her part and begs Ines not to repeat the town's silence. At the qualifier, Ines deliberately loses his heat to stay near the old wing. Emotional beat: sacrifice over glory.

chapters.title: Read the Names
chapters.summary: Climax at the championship: Ines swims, then stops mid-race, takes the microphone, and reads Marisol Vann's name and the names of every student scrubbed from Cedar Falls' records as the crowd goes silent and the lockers swing open. Resolution: an investigation reopens, the demolition halts, and grandma's recipe box gains one new card — written by Ines, addressed forward. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into witness.
